title: C4109A — Rear subwoofer amplifier connector
introduction:
I use this reference to connect the rear subwoofer amplifier’s cavity drawing with its circuit and parts information. The function labels separate the amplifier’s enable connection, ground, fuse-or-circuit-breaker supply connection and audio pair. Think of enable as the invitation to play; the audio connections carry the musical conversation.

Start with the connector identity table, find a cavity label in the drawing, then read across its matching assignment row. Finish with the parts tables if you need to understand the listed service identifiers. This is a reading guide: physical viewing direction, access, electrical test conditions and replacement methods are outside its scope. Keep Gauge, Size and Used entries as printed without assigning an unsupported convention or meaning.

edits.why: I use the housing outline, staggered cavity positions and central rectangular feature to keep my place in this drawing. Gray-filled positions correspond to rows with blank circuit and function entries; outlined positions correspond to populated rows. That agreement helps cross-check the drawing against this table without establishing a physical viewing direction.

Cavity links each drawing label to a table row. Read across that row to connect the circuit identifier with its color, gauge, function and terminal part number. The function column distinguishes enable, supply, ground and audio roles; it does not show that any connection is electrically healthy. The fuse-or-circuit-breaker wording identifies a function, not a current rating.

The pigtail table connects the listed kit with its service assembly and engineering shell. Its Gauge and Material fields describe the pigtail entry; the assignment table describes individual circuit rows. I keep those lookup purposes separate rather than treating the pigtail specification as a replacement specification for every wire.
